exec.shell: No shell is inserted. A caller may still explicitly name a shell in argv, so a future ProjectRun contract must close bootstrap authority separately.

v1Contract.lifecycle: request-owned ID plus consuming capability tokens; create, exact policy readiness, prepare/commit execution, delete, and terminal absence
v1Contract.serviceBoundary: strict versioned JSON framing, mTLS caller authorization, asset-bundle identity, durable lifecycle records, restart reconciliation, cancellation, and drain
v1Contract.result: real nonnegative exit, bounded raw stdout/stderr, timeout observation, proxy egress decisions, and optional stable OS-denial categories

providers.srt: OpenBox-owned macOS Seatbelt or Linux bubblewrap adapter with a compiled hash-pinned profile
providers.openShell: explicit external gateway adapter pinned to one source revision

v1Contract.productionClient: not exported; SandboxRuntimeClient is cfg(test) only
v1Contract.launcherBoundary: obs is a separate operator launcher, not the production sandbox service

projectRunGaps: no content-addressed project snapshot upload or source manifest
no dependency preparation, cache identity, or immutable prepared image contract
no declared non-secret environment or scoped secret references
no receiver, fixture, model relay, or multi-service topology
no readiness path, stimulus protocol, or project-level session lifecycle
no process-count budget in the request
no project artifact, receipt, or normalized evidence retrieval
no project-level redaction or retention contract
no production client surface available to Shift Left
threatAssumptions: The service configuration, compiled profile, policy identity, asset bundle, caller certificates, and durable store are trusted deployment inputs.
V1 creates a fresh empty request-owned workspace and never mounts or copies a developer worktree.
V1 never inherits ambient environment or secrets; adding those to CreateRequest or ExecRequest would weaken the existing boundary.
Raw bounded stdout and stderr may contain caller content; V1 does not provide the Shift Left redacted-digests retention guarantee.
macOS SRT can constrain direct sockets to its exact proxy port; Linux network-enabled SRT cannot provide the same direct-socket guarantee without another kernel control.
OpenShell live behavior depends on an external provisioned gateway/image/policy/mTLS tuple; source and skipped tests are not live proof.
Cleanup authority is retained structurally after possible creation/dispatch and must remain fail-closed across any future protocol.

testLedger.observations: 86 library tests passed, including strict protocol, lifecycle, mTLS boundary, durable reconciliation, failure invariants, and unchanged twenty-scenario conformance suites.

testLedger.command: cargo test --test live_srt as part of cargo test --all-features
testLedger.observations: The real native lifecycle/argv/timeout/cleanup test passed. The proxy-denial and denied-write tests failed because sandbox violation evidence was absent: DeniedNetwork was missing and violation Option was None. Confinement effects were not promoted into denial-log proof.
All three test functions returned after explicit SKIP messages because OPENBOX_LIVE_OPENSHELL_ENDPOINT and the exact gateway tuple were not configured; their cargo status 0 is not live evidence.
Formatting and lint gates passed on the clean exact commit.

decisionBoundary.recommendationAtThisTask: Preserve v1 byte/behavior compatibility and carry its strict lifecycle/evidence primitives into provider-neutral ProjectRun requirements; do not claim current project fit.
